messages.subject: runModels on linux
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm using R on linux (3.0.1) with mplus through wine (though I've created the alias "mplus" for "wine mplus"). When I try to use runModels, it looks like it tries to run the following system command (notice quotes): cd "/home/correct/directory" && "mplus" "model.inp" . When it runs, I get the error: sh: mplus: command not found. If I try running the same system command, with quotes in the same place (i.e., system(command="cd '/home/correct/directory' && 'mplus' 'model.inp'")) I get the same error, but if I run the same command removing all the quotes (i.e., system(command="cd /home/correct/directory && mplus model.inp") then the model runs (I can also use the command line from the directory and successfully run the model using "mplus" or "wine plus"). Any thoughts?

Thanks!

Rich

messages.subject: Re: runModels on linux
messages.body_plain:
Actually, now looking through the code for runModels() I see that it doesn't use that system command that it echoes (or at least I think it doesn't). It looks like it is using system2(). However, as far as I can tell, this is problematic with mplus with wine. Again, I can run "wine mplus model.inp" from the command line and successfully run my models. I can also use system() from within R with the command "wine mplus model.inp". However, it looks like system2 can only take one word for the command. So, for instance, system2(command="wine", args="mplus model.inp") works, but system2(command="wine mplus", args="model.inp") does not. I also tried to create a one-word system-wide alias for "wine mplus", so that when I run from the command line, just running "mplus model.inp" works. But for some reason, this doesn't seem to work either from system() or system2() (I think I was wrong in my original post when I said that the alias worked with system()).

messages.subject: Re: readModels bug with 10 class GMM
messages.body_plain:
Hi Patrick,

Thanks for attaching the output that was not reading properly into MplusAutomation. You're right that the issue was with extracting class counts from models that contain many classes. What was happening is that the class counts output was wrapping across paragraphs (classes 1-9 were in one group, class 10 in another). I hadn't previously seen this output format before, so the package wasn't interpreting it appropriately. I have now updated the package to handle this circumstance and your output reads in appropriately. As a bonus, the package now also obtains the classification probabilities and logits, which were present in your file.

To get this fix, install the development version of MplusAutomation using:

install.packages("devtools")
require(devtools)

install_github("MplusAutomation", "michaelhallquist")
library(MplusAutomation)

Let me know if you have any other problems.

Best,
Michael

messages.subject_clean: Save additional estimates in output (from a mediation model)
messages.body_plain:
This is a great program! I am using Mplus to test indirect effects in many path models, and just used Mplus Automation for the first time this week!

Is it possible to save the estimates from the total, direct, and indirect effects section of the output? I can obtain the parameter estimates from the OLS and probit regressions. But I'd especially like to obtain the estimates of the indirect effects.

Thanks.
Cathy

messages.subject: Re: Save additional estimates in output (from a mediation model)
messages.subject_clean: Save additional estimates in output (from a mediation model)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Cathy,

At this point, the package does not read the output of MODEL INDIRECT, so the total, direct, and indirect effects sections are not available in R. Others have asked for this feature, too, and it's on my "to do" list. The problem is that this section is pretty variable in its format, which makes it hard to parse, but I have worked on it a bit. With luck, this feature will come out in late summer. Other contributors to this effort are welcome, if you're interested.

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: runModels on linux
messages.body_plain:
Just to follow up, I think that replacing line 442 of runModels.R (and presumably the corresponding line for the interactive function) with the following should work:

      if (Mplus_command=="wine mplus") {
          s2command <- "wine"
          s2args <- paste("mplus",inputSplit$filename,sep=" ")
      } else {
          s2command <- Mplus_command
          s2args <- c(shQuote(inputSplit$filename))
      }
      exitCode <- system2(s2command, args=s2args, stdout=stdout.value, wait=TRUE)

Perhaps there is some other workaround when using wine, but this worked for me.

Also, on line 441, you have      setwd(inputSplit$directory)

But isn't this NA sometimes? It caused an error for me when running runModels() without specifying a directory (though this happened after messing with the code for runModels.R, so perhaps it was a side effect of something else I did). For the windows command, it seems that you switch to "dirtocd" which defaults to the working directory if inputSplit$directory is NA.

Finally, am I correct that you cannot currently pass a different Mplus_command to mplusModeler?

I also tried to create a one-word system-wide alias for "wine mplus", so that when I run from the command line, just running "mplus model.inp" works. But for some reason, this doesn't seem to work either from system() or system2() (I think I was wrong in my original post when I said that the alias worked with system()).

messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] Re: runModels on linux
messages.body_plain:
Hi Richard,

You are correct for now that you cannot pass a different Mplus_command
to mplusModeler.  That is an easy change to make though.

Regarding your other comments on wine, I am less sure.  There is an
Mplus version for Linux, so to my knowledge we have not tried to run
the windows version on Linux via wine.

I have opened two issues on github
(https://github.com/michaelhallquist/MplusAutomation/issues?state=open)
and will fix them sooner or later.

Thanks for your interest!

Joshua
